quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 EMS and other results: EMS revenue TWD 65.8 billion (+6% QoQ, +12% YoY), EMS gross margin 8.9% (-0.6 points QoQ), operating margin 2.4%, EMS operating profit TWD 1.6 billion; EMS profitability was slightly below expectations on product mix and higher component prices, and EMS computing growth is largely driven by AI accelerator products. ATM gross profit TWD 34.5 billion and operating profit TWD 19.8 billion (+25% QoQ, +124% YoY); ATM operating expense ratio 11.7%, expected to continue to improve in the back half of 2026. Q2 facilities spending TWD 658 million. CFO Joseph Tung: Q3 EMS revenue growth of around 40% QoQ is 'a little bit abnormal seasonality', largely because of component price hikes, particularly in memory (a pass-through cost); excluding them Q3 EMS operating margin would be around 3.7%, 3.8%; Q4 EMS revenue at a pretty similar level to Q3; full-year EMS growth 'just sub-20%', and he confirmed 35%+ growth for the ATM business.
quarterly_data.figure: EMS revenue TWD 65.8B (+12% YoY), EMS OM 2.4%; Q3 EMS ~40% QoQ on memory price hikes; FY EMS sub-20%; ATM 35%+

quarterly_data.signal: SYSTEM-LEVEL STRATEGY (IR head Ken Hsiang): at holding-company level ASE continues to pursue synergies between its ATM and EMS businesses to co-develop system-level solutions, particularly in optical interconnects, power delivery and thermal management, applying the co-engineering disciplines that scaled its SiP architecture; the AI build-out 'will require unprecedented hardware capacity and capability expansion. At this point, we are just trying to keep up.' COO Dr. Tien Wu: AI demands new hardware in size, complexity and integration, and there is a growing need for industrial power, connectivity and storage devices that ASE is seeing 'from all of our customers on the multi-year basis'. On CPO, Dr. Wu on the hybrid of electrical and optical signals: 'I think that direction is definitive' — the question is when and how to execute; ASE has been working on it for about 20 years.

FOUNDRY PARTNERSHIP AND FULL PROCESS (COO Dr. Tien Wu): the collaboration with the lead foundry partner is long-term — a pure-play wafer foundry with a pure-play packaging house, with a clear boundary; some packaging must be taken by the foundry 'because access to the leading-edge wafer is simply not available to the others' or because of strict customer IP, and otherwise the collaboration covers all aspects of packaging — OS, full process, 'the full spectrum'. Full process: 'we do have line of sight', tracking nicely, also for 2027, with full visibility on the capacity being developed; ASE's 'clientele portfolio covers all of them' (GPU, CPU, ASIC), 'in two quarters time, we should be able to give you' the 2027 LEAP services revenue and its OS / full process / assembly / test split, while on GPU / CPU / ASIC customers 'we need a little bit more time to digest how much information we can share'. On EMIB, ASE is also collaborating with other customers 'along the same line, including EMIB'. CFO Joseph Tung: the stronger demand forecast is coming 'not just customers, but also our foundry partner', and ASE is entering new projects, new products and new process steps.

CFO Joseph Tung on margins: improvement comes from margin-accretive business growth, efficiency gains, continued expansion of automated factories and operating leverage on volume growth, with the OpEx ratio continuing to drop on an annual basis; 'we should be continue to see our margin expansion on a sequential basis, at least for this year and next', and once past the structural margin range ASE will review it and 'see how far we can go'. On investment: 'we are not going to be shy in making the necessary investment, not just to support our customer, but also to maintain our clear leadership position in this field.'
